assumptions: Onset was placed at 14:09 by the investigating agent from per-minute metrics; the alert itself did not fire until 14:14:46, so the pre-alert portion of the impact window is inferred rather than alerted on.
The flag revert is treated as causal because the service returned to baseline shortly after it; this is a temporal correlation, not an isolated test.

The defective code path is assumed to have been present but dormant before 14:09 on the basis that the change log shows no deploy on the service in the prior two days. The change log was only queried back that far plus a 255-minute window; a deploy outside those windows would not have been seen.
The specific input condition that produces the division by zero at spend_summary.py:32 was never established — only the exception and its location were observed.

The low-rate UpstreamTimeout errors on account pages seen throughout the hour before onset are assumed to be pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident; they were not investigated and were still present after mitigation.
The proposed fix is an unreviewed draft pull request; it has not been verified to resolve the defect.
Recovery was judged from the service returning to baseline within the mitigation agent's wait window; no follow-up check beyond 14:16:03 is recorded.
input.executive_summary: On 17 September 2026, a newly enabled feature on the online shop caused a share of customers' account pages to fail to load. The feature began reaching customers at about 14:09 UTC and was on for everyone by 14:10; account page failures rose immediately and stayed elevated. An automated alert fired at 14:14:46, the on-call automation investigated, identified the newly enabled feature as the cause, and turned it back off at 14:15:11. The shop returned to its normal behaviour by 14:16:03, when recovery was confirmed. Total customer-visible impact ran from roughly 14:09 to 14:16 UTC. Only account pages were affected; browsing, checkout and other parts of the shop were not implicated. A draft code change to fix the underlying defect was opened at 14:16:44 and still needs review and merge before the feature can be safely enabled again.
input.root_cause: Enabling the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop exposed a latent division-by-zero in the new spend-summary code path (`ZeroDivisionError` at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32), which threw on account page renders; the flag went from fully off to a partial rollout at 14:09 and fully on at 14:10, and account-page errors tracked that ramp exactly. No deployment was recorded on the service in the preceding two days, so the code was already shipped and dormant behind the flag — the flag flip, not a release, was the trigger.
